strengths: The paper addresses a useful computer vision problem: discovering relevant class names automatically for open-vocabulary segmentation. Captioning clustered BLIP features provides a concrete mechanism that can guide existing segmenters without additional training.

Table 1 provides encouraging evidence for local captioning: SELF-SEG improves class-agnostic mIoU over BLIP plus X-Decoder from 38.0 to 41.9 on VOC, 26.7 to 29.2 on ADE20K, and 29.2 to 35.8 on CityScapes.

The overall pipeline is clearly explained, pretrained models and datasets are attributed, and several implementation parameters and evaluator prompts are provided. The appendix usefully acknowledges hallucinated nouns, overly generic descriptions, and competition between related labels.
weaknesses: The validity of LOVE, which determines the reported semantic scores, is insufficiently established. Appendix A instructs the LLM to map stuff descriptions to background even for CityScapes and ADE20K, which contain valid stuff categories. The exact-match override only partially addresses this problem. For ADE20K, the evaluator additionally relies on the LLM knowing the vocabulary rather than supplying all 847 classes. No human audit, mapping-accuracy measurement, or quantitative comparison with alternative evaluators establishes how these choices affect results.

The headline comparisons do not establish a common evaluation protocol. Table 2 reports 41.6 versus 20.1 mIoU against ZeroSeg on VOC, but does not demonstrate that ZeroSeg was evaluated using LOVE and identical class/background handling. Differences in pretrained components and supervision also complicate attribution of this gain. No competing automatic-class method is reported on ADE20K or CityScapes, leaving the state-of-the-art claims on those datasets weakly supported.

The experiments only partially isolate the proposed contribution. The plain-caption baseline is evaluated using class-agnostic mIoU, which ignores label correctness, rather than the final semantic metric. A matched caption-generation budget is not established. Comparisons with simple regional captioning and ablations of multiscale clustering, cross-clustering alignment, and denoising would help determine whether the gains specifically require the proposed machinery.

Parameter selection may introduce optimistic reporting. Section 4.1 states that parameters were optimized for VOC mIoU without identifying a separate tuning split. Tables 2 and 3 use the best caption-cycle count for each evaluated dataset, again without describing independent selection. This choice matters substantially: CityScapes changes from 27.4 with one cycle to 41.1 with twenty. Repeated-run variability is also absent despite stochastic caption generation.

Secondary reproducibility and practical-efficiency gaps remain. Equation 10 describes independent maximum-IoU assignments rather than the stated Hungarian matching, and alignment between the two spatial resolutions is underspecified. Runtime and memory measurements are missing despite repeated decoding over multiple clusters and up to twenty-five captioning cycles.
